hypothesis: Pair the same convex top feature on B and D in red and the concave right feature on B and E in blue. This partial feature substitution can wrongly make D seem redundant while keeping B.
marker_roles: B top convex arc is paired with D top convex arc; these are actual congruent source features.
D top convex arc is the second member of the red feature match, not an isolated answer contour.
B right concave arc is paired with E right concave arc.
E right concave arc is the second member of the blue match. The two roles together tempt a false B-for-D substitution, ignoring B extra concavity.
primary_math_review: Curved-edge counts (convex,concave): A=(0,2),B=(1,1),C=(2,0),D=(1,0),E=(0,1). Straight square boundary requires curved edges paired convex to concave. Only omitting B balances three with three; A,C,D,E can form a square by pairing C two convex with A two concave and D convex with E concave. B is uniquely excluded. Open arc recolorings add no piece or cut and preserve all tangents/endpoints.
